# SPD-088 — Bash hook: an arithmetic command ((...)) is read as a redirection, so '(( n > 2 ))' is refused as a write to a file named 2

## Brief
Both shells evaluate '(( ... ))' as arithmetic: the '>' inside it is a comparison and no file is opened. The hook tokenizes the parentheses away and separate_redirects then reads the '>' as an output operator and the word after it as a target, so a plain arithmetic command is refused as a write. It was already so for a non-digit operand on main -- '(( a > b ))' records the target b and '(( n >= 3 ))' the target '=' -- and SPD-045, which stops the hook dropping a digit or '-' operand as a descriptor, adds the common literal forms '(( n > 2 ))' and '(( i > 0 ))' to the same set. A member writing 'if (( retries > 3 )); then' is now refused wherever the shell's directory is outside its deliverables, and so is Spud in a protected one. Narrow and mechanical, but it costs a member a form it has every reason to write. The fix belongs where the parentheses are still visible -- prepare/zsh/walk, outside SPD-049's deliverable globs -- so it was not widened into that ticket.

Evidence: analyse_command on the working tree (SPD-049, wave 3): '(( 3 > 2 ))' records redirects ['2'], 'if (( n > 2 )); then echo x; fi' ['2'], 'x=$(( 1 > 2 ))' ['2'], 'if (( i > 0 )); then true; fi' ['0'], and on main as well as here '(( n >= 3 ))' ['='] and '(( a > b ))' ['b']; 'let "n > 2"' and '[[ 3 -gt 2 ]]' record none. The SPD-049 differential (6007 command lines before and after, the whole test suite's string constants plus the four tickets' own) shows 'x=$(( 1<2 )); (( 3 > 2 )) && echo y' as one of the 32 member lines that went silent -> deny. Fix sketch: mark the tokens between '((' and '))' (and inside a '$(( ))' arithmetic expansion) as arithmetic when the line is prepared, the way mark_zsh_patterns marks zsh's own glob operators, so separate_redirects never sees the comparison as an operator; pin it with '(( n > 2 ))', '(( n >= 3 ))' and '(( a > b ))' silent for a member, and a real redirection after an arithmetic command still checked.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer spudagent on opus, no children: the fix is narrow and mechanical (mark the tokens of an arithmetic command and an arithmetic expansion so separate_redirects never reads a comparison as an operator), but it sits on the hook path in prepare/zsh/walk, where a wrong reading refuses a member a form it has every reason to write. opus rather than the fable tier a reviewer would take: the work is implementation against an evidence-rich brief, and the whole suite plus the hook-timing probe are the check.
